answer: Agents could admit new participants only after an existing member locks a bond that is forfeited if the newcomer double-spends or colludes in a provable fraud. Each identity must also earn a rate-limited share of trade history before it can sponsor another, so minting thousands of names does not multiply influence. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital and risk losing it, while waiting for each identity to build history. A copper ledger, lotus market, or whisper network cannot make those costs disappear.
